why: Press (Phalcon/BlockSec via Quadriga, Peapods' thank-you message) says Yoink front-ran the attacker's second attempt. On chain the attacker (EOA 0x277da2d1) succeeded on pair 1 at block 22873986 idx 4 (+78.19 ETH), then tried the USDC pair 0xca1154bb in blocks 22874007/08/09 (txs 0xdc774417, 0x505db202, 0xa03582cc); each pair-2 leg reverted inside the attacker's try/catch. Yoink's tx 0xff8e9226 (block 22874010 idx 0, 12 s after the last attempt) has the same 42 state-changing calls (role-normalised similarity 1.0, same 10M USDC Morpho loan, same swap sizes) and its borrow passed, taking 174,258.31 USDC (11.4944 ETH to coinbase, no builder refund). No attacker tx is shown pending: the attempts had already landed, the attacker's calldata on the pre-Yoink state still reverts (debug_traceCall), and none of either side's txs is in the mempool archive. Yoink adapted and completed a failed, already-mined attack; it did not pre-empt anything we can show. Yoink returned 126,891.81 USDC (90% after recouping 33,267 USDC for its stated 11.95 ETH bribe).
strength: replay/adaptation is shown call-for-call; 'no pending tx' is an absence of evidence (both sides private flow), and why the attacker's borrow reverts while Yoink's passes is undetermined
